*_All categories:_*

*How can I select which categories I would like to receive trips for?*

If the driver is registered in more than one category, they can manage which categories they will receive trips for via the app. First, the driver will need to go online. Once online, click on the vehicle icon and make the selections as they wish. Drivers can change their categories in the app as often as they wish. 

*_XL category:_*

*How can I disable Bolt category trips to receive XL trips only?*

The driver cannot permanently opt-out of Standard trips if his car has the XL category enabled. However, drivers can manage which categories they wish to receive trips for in the app. To manage which categories are active, the driver should go online and then click on the vehicle icon, then select/deselect their preferred categories.

Good morning,

The amount of data seems (without more explanation) excessive. I would recommend to ask for more details and a proper legal bases. It is not our duty to find the proper legal bases for the authority that requested the data. Personal data that is processed by the Malta Police is regulated primarily by Legal Notice 168 of 2018 Data Protection (Processing of Personal Data by Competent Authorities for the Purposes of the Prevention, Investigation, Detection of Prosecution of Criminal Offences or the execution of Criminal Penalties) Regulation, the Data Protection Act (Chapter 586 of the Laws of Malta) and Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and the Council of 27th April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (NOT in Chapter 440).

If PI Frendo is providing the necessary informations, I would also make sure, that the Data is not transferred by mail. Law enforcement agencies should be able to provide a proper and secure channel to deliver it:

_"Dear PI George Frendo,_

_We endeavor to comply with your request as soon as possible within the framework of the legal requirements. Due to the type, amount and heterogeneity of the required personal data, the data protection team was included as part of the processing of your request._

_After consulting our data protection team and in order to check the data protection conformity of the request at Bolt and to document it accordingly, I politely ask you to provide the following additional information:_

* _Is the processing of personal data to the requested extent and type necessary for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties?_ 
* _In terms of section 8(1) of Legal Notice 168 of 2018 Data Protection (Processing of Personal Data by Competent Authorities for the Purposes of the Prevention, Investigation, Detection of Prosecution of Criminal Offences or the execution of Criminal Penalties) Regulation processing shall be lawful only if it is based on law. We may ask you to provide the concrete legal basis for the processing (specification of the relevant law including the exact article or section) prior to transmission._
* _The request is directed to a large number of possible data subjects and data categories. Taking into account Section 4(1) lit c f Legal Notice 168 of 2018 Data Protection (Processing of Personal Data by Competent Authorities for the Purposes of the Prevention, Investigation, Detection of Prosecution of Criminal Offences or the execution of Criminal Penalties) Regulation, we ask for a statement as to whether and to what extent the collection of the requested data is appropriate, relevant and not excessive with regard to the purposes for which it is processed._
* With reference to the general principle of data minimization, I may ask you to describe the requested data to the relevant and necessary degree.
* _Regarding the case reference number, I am sorry to inform you that it is not visible on the letter sent. I therefore request that you provide the case number._

_You also asked for a soft copy medium. Can the Malta police force provide a data protection-compliant and secure transmission channel? If not, which format and which transmission channel are preferred?”_

Hi [~accountid:6168449c2f6aed0068375106] - thanks for raising this ticket.

These heads of terms are very odd and defective. It doesn’t sound like the landlord knows what it is doing. The following points should (re)considered:

(1) Is this for an unmanned office? Please confirm.

(2) This arrangement is stated to be a ‘12 month term that rolls over’. I will assume that this is a 12 month term with the benefit of the statutory continuation provisions of the LTA 1954. We can stay silent on this point for now and see what they give to us. FYI a lease (being an interest in property) typically comes with an obligation to to repair the internal parts are the premises, hence…

(3) … it’s very odd that the HOTs say that the Landlord is responsible for all repairs (?\!). This is fine from our perspective, but no sensible Landlord would agree this. How did this arise? In any case, we can stay silent on this for now. 

(4) Have we not asked for a break option? As mentioned, we should not sign up to long arrangements that we have no ability to get out of. At first instance I suggest we ask for the ability to terminate the arrangement at 3 month’s notice.

(5) Are we not contributing towards service charge and insurance? You would typically do so in a lease arrangement. We can stay silent on this point for now. 

(6) The “Statutory Obligations” section is simply wrong, particularly with regards to asbestos (as this statutory obligation only vests only if we are obliged to repair or make good the premises). We can agree that: “The tenant is to be responsible for complying with all statutory obligations which may apply by virtue of the tenancy by law (including any pursuant to the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2006 and the Control of Substances Hazardous to HealthRegulations 2002)”.

(7) The User clause is defective, it should never specific a use specific for a tenant (because it would bind assignees - therefore the lease becomes un-assignable by virtue of this use). This should specify ‘office use only’.

Points 4, 6 and 7 will need picking up with the landlord. Let me know your thoughts on the others. Thanks.

*Please do not send this letter to the NBU.*

Some background.

There is a risk that our normal payment flow (where we collect fees from users and forward them to drivers, less our fees) would be qualified as the provision of payment services and require us to obtain a license in almost all of the jurisdictions we operate - regardless of whether the funds are collected by Bolt Operations or a local entity. In the EU, we rely on the commercial agent exemption, saying that we act as a collection agent for the drivers and, as such, should not be required to obtain a license to provide payment services. In other jurisdictions, it has not been analyzed what the potential exemptions we could rely on are - if any. 

However, *as a general approach, we should currently refrain from approaching any single financial supervision authority with this question - unless we take a global decision to do otherwise*. 

Asking a financial supervision authority for their opinion, without giving them reasoning on why we ourselves are absolutely certain that there is an exemption in applicable laws which would allow us not to apply for a license, would likely result in: (a) the financial supervision authority saying that we will indeed need to apply for a license; or alternatively, (b) result in the authority coming back with a somewhat ignorant but often seen answer that they do not provide legal opinions on any particular business model - and potentially a reference saying that if we think we need a license we should apply for one, in which case the authority would assess our case and a reference saying that unlicensed provision of payment services is subject to penalties. 

In any case, *we do not want to approach any supervisory authority without detailed argumentation on why we think we will not need a license.*

It is intended that we make a decision in January on whether to apply for a license to provide payment services. If we do, then we will probably obtain a license in an EU jurisdiction and thereafter, to the extent necessary, in other jurisdictions. It is possible that we would then engage on obtaining legal opinions from law firms from each of the jurisdictions where we have business to assess whether our payment activities in such jurisdiction would need a license - in which case we might apply for a license in such jurisdiction as well. However, it is possible that our approach will be to rely on an interpretation that our normal payment flow should not be considered the provision of payment services in any relevant jurisdiction and we would not apply for a license in such jurisdiction.

In any case, *unless we are not applying for a license, we should refrain from approaching any financial supervision authority without specific argumentation on why we believe we do not need a license*.

I hope we will have a global approach on this approved by our management by the end of January.

Until then, if necessary, we could obtain a legal opinion from a local law firm to give us comfort that we do not need a license - or certainty that we do. But we could as well ask for such legal opinions from every single one of our jurisdictions around the world. So, as per the current approach of relying on the presumption that our normal payment flow does not need a license, we would need some specific reasoning to obtain such an opinion from Ukraine. 

Therefore, *is anything waiting on clarity over this matter?* Is Citi refusing to proceed with any of our requests because of this matter? Let me know and I can proceed with obtaining an opinion. But if there are no particular reasons other than slight doubt on whether we need a license, then I would refrain from obtaining an opinion.

And in any case, *we should refrain from approaching the NBU with the suggested letter.*

Summarizing a call we had today with [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3] @carolina and @david: 

* *_Background_*: We have a Passenger claiming a case of fraud and data breach in PT (saying that someone hacked their account using their old phone number). However we think it's just a case of 'recycled phone number'. Passenger is complaining about unknown charges (EUR 430).
* *_Global T&Cs_*: We normally have grounds to argue that it's the Passengers' responsibility to notify us when they change their mobile number and that there is no GDPR breach - based on clause 1.3 of our Global T&Cs _(If the user is no longer using their mobile number, they must notify Bolt within 7 days, so that Bolt can archive the account. It is also stated that if the user does not notify us about any change to their number, the user mobile operator may issue the same mobile number to a new person who then using the Bolt app may have access to the user's data)._ 
*_PT T&Cs_*: However, for some unexplained reason, there is a disparity between our Global T&Cs and the PT T&Cs. Clause 3.1 of the PT T&Cs  just states that: _the user has to create and account with username and password -->_ However this is not the case as the account creation is connected to the mobile number and entering the confirmation code received by SMS. There is no mention in the PT T&Cs of having to inform us in case of a change of mobile number. [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3] and I agree that *we have therefore no ground to argue that it was the passenger's responsibility to inform us and therefore we see no other way but to pay the EUR 430* (which actually shows that we are kind of admitting that Bolt did something wrong and we’re afraid this might create a precedent...).

Hey there Lana. 

Marking the order/payment never actually blocked the card from being used again. The marking just flags the payment and adds a risk score to the user. If the customer wants to prevent more charges from coming from the card, the only way to do it is to reach the bank and block it.

Regarding how to deal with such cases, you should still follow steps from the article:

* Inform the reporter that we have taken internal measures to solve this issue (do not disclose what exactly)
* Advise the user that if they want further information, they can contact their bank for more details about the situation.

Changes in the whole unknown charges procedure are planned for Q1. One of the ideas is to mark the card once an unknown charge is reported, then we kill the card, preventing more charges. But until the development is done, please just keep following the current article. If it’s really an unknown charge, the user will reach the bank and we’ll get the notification of fraud from the issuer, which will mark the payment anyway. Our internal marking is just a faster way to flag the payment and user before the actual payment issue arrives.

Unlike the DSAs for Wolfsburg, *our local counsel (Andersen) flagged an issue with this one for Düsseldorf.* Please see their advice below:

“Stadtverwaltung Düsseldorf *reserves the right to evaluate, aggregate, merge with other data sources, analyze, classify, or otherwise process the submitted data with the aim of using the data for the agreed  purposes* (see sec. 3 para 2). Pursuant to sec. 1 para 2 those are _inter alia_:

* “Verification of compliance with agreements within the framework of the special use permit and punishment of violations;”
* “Manage, analyze, plan, direct, and optimize transportation and mobility services within the city limits, including enforcement of regulations and policies;”

From our perspective, this triggers the applicability of GDPR, because data is not anonymized but pseudonymized and a person could possibly be determined with the use of additional information the “Stadtverwaltung Düsseldorf” holds. In this case the processing activity requires a legal basis pursuant to article 6 GDPR as well as the information of affected individuals via the data privacy statement (see article 13 GDPR).

 There are 3 ways to resolve the issue as follows:

a) Limit the aggregation right to cases where Bolt would be legally obliged to disclose personal data pursuant to article 6 para 1 lit. c GDPR;

b) Ask customers for consent regarding the data transfer and properly inform them as required by article 7 GDPR;

c) Cancel sec. 3 para 2 of the DSA, refer to the legal obligation to disclose personal data in case of lawful disclosure requests and prohibit the merging with additional data.

Option c) is our preferred path the resolve this matter. In the event Stadtverwaltung Düsseldorf pushes back in that respect, you could make use of option a) as fall back position. At least, that would be a compromise as Stadtverwaltung Düsseldorf will in general be able to aggregate the pseudonymized data, but only to the extent under which Bolt would be legally required  to disclose the relevant data.”

If the video surveillance is put in place for security reasons then this is okay under the legitimate interest legal basis under GDPR. If there should be any country specific regulation then we can adjust the approach but in EU countries we have approached as following:

It is okay to use video surveillance for the following purposes:

* Control the access to the premises and to ensure the security of the premises, including the safety of our property, information and employees. 
* To prevent and if necessary, investigate unauthorised access to secure premises and protected areas. 
* To prevent, detect and investigate theft and property damages or threats to the safety of the employees working in the premises.  

It is prohibited to use video surveillance system for any other purpose, such as to monitor the work of employees or their attendance. +This means that there should be no live monitoring on the employees for the purpose of checking the performance of their duties.+ 

The conditions to keep in mind:

# *Positioning the cameras*

The location and positioning of the video cameras has to take into account the legitimate expectations of the data subject to their privacy. Therefore monitoring is not to be expected in recreational areas, sanitary areas, changing rooms etc.

*2. Retention period*

All personal data processed must have a retention period. No personal data should be kept indefinitely, so a proportionate and reasoned retention time must be set for keeping this data. 

Retention period must be determined depending on the purpose why this data is being collected. 

Data can be stored for no longer than it is necessary for the purposes for which it was collected (e.g the market practice for storing this data is 30-60 days, but can be shorter or longer depending on the need). 

After the retention period, recordings must be deleted automatically (overwritten by new video footage). 

*3. Warning signs of video surveillance*

*3.1 Position of the warning sign.* 
It is obligatory to install warning signs on the premises where video surveillance is carried out. The information should be positioned in such a way that the data subject can easily recognise the circumstances of the surveillance before entering the monitored area (approximately at eye level). 

*3.2* *Content of the warning sign.* 

The warning sign/sticker can be as following:

Camera picture/”we have video surveillance”

_Purpose: Safety of people and property_
_Legal basis: legitimate interest_
_Controller: Bolt Operations OÜ_
_Detailed information:_ [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance/] or QR code to the page

It’s a combination of many reasons - as of 2021 when we grant stock we calculate the amount how many units can be granted based on annual salary and if the employee has any previous grants then we also take these into account, looking at the historic value of these grants. The overall logic is that we should be looking at total comp, monthly salary and value of granted options, not only monthly salary and then put some amount of options on top.

As you know then in the past we have not done so, and especially in CS there were specific amount of units given to specific positions for years while it was not though through what’s the valuation of each grant. Here’s an example: if someone joined at the beginning of 2018 and got 80 units then their grant was worth either 504€ (unit value 6.3€), if they joined at the end of 2018 the same amount of units was worth 2944€ (unit value 36.8€). The same amount of units granted today is worth 18 400€\! Looking at the numbers and how our valuation has grown then we cannot base option grants on units but need to think of the actual value of the grant, as this is also money that Bolt is giving out.

We are getting regular unknown charge tickets “help, somebody stole my money, I did not pay for this”, and there is “[FOOD.BOLT.EU|http://FOOD.BOLT.EU]” in the bank statement, so they turn to us.

We do a regular investigation as if it’s a normal unknown charge, based on the card, we find connected accounts, but you cannot find the Bolt Balance top-up in Admin 1’s Payments.
Based on the “directory” (see the attachment) of the payment, we usually know where to somehow look, if it’s a Rides or Food issue, but when it comes to “/C/”, there is no official KB recommendation.

The way you can find out which connected account used the card, and topped up (stole) money for their own account is: You go to Admin 2 (which is not connected to Rider/Eater profiles in Admin 1), find the Bolt Balance, fill in the Rider/Eater user IDs of the connected accounts, and investigate the BB differences. 
Sometimes, it’s a user from another country, so there is even a different currency, so you have to take the amount from the bank statement and google the amount in the other currency because the Bolt Balance is localised.

Since Admin 1 profile is not connected (there is no button to simply jump into Admin 2) to the Bolt Balance section of the specific user, I doubt Fraud can track these cases before they happen (I might be wrong, and it’s just an UI problem for the Customer Support). That was just advised as a caution for a potentially bigger problem.

When it comes to the Admin link, sometimes, the other person just tops up the credits (steals money), and doesn’t make new orders/rides, so there is no Admin link to be shown. If we get the report, we block the user according to KB.

The problem is the complicated investigation (Bolt Balance in Admin 2 is a broken page, and it’s quite hard to read), which is not currently included in the KB article.

Hope this made it a bit more clear, please do ask more questions if not\!

Dear All,

First, I would like to apologies for not responding earlier and not providing any updates. The matter has turned out to be more complex and nuanced than initially assessed.

After several discussions and analysis with external counsels we came to conclusion that the general rule must be that +the automatic deduction of traffic fines/contractual penalties cannot be done without user’s prior consent.+  Implementing automatic deduction without user’s consent poses legal risks (there is no clear legal framework for this), requires very precise and detailed regulation (and even then, Bolt may be challenged that the regulation is void standard term), continuing updates to T&C’s, user flow requiring individual approaches to users, etc. and ultimately may result in pad publicity.

The option is to deduct a traffic fine/contractual penalty*** up to EUR 500 from the user’ payment method once user’s consent has received. Below it is described how to implement this option. From technical point of view, it probably needs creating and implementing some new technical solutions and features in the app, therefore requires consulting with rental’s product and engineering team. The approach should be walked through also with Commerce team.

First, BD T&C-s requires an update. Please see adjustments made to the T&C’s and the List of Penalties with track changes function.

+The user flow should be following+:

# The user commits an action or omission which results in fine/contractual penalty/damaged defined and explained below under the “***”.
# the user receives *an e-mail from Bolt* (see point 3 of the attached User Flow Notifications);
# in parallel to the e-mail, the user receives a *push notification* (see point 1 of the attached User Flow Notifications) and by clicking on it, the user sees a page in the Bolt app for *Bolt in app notification* (see point 2 of the attached User Flow Notifications) where the user can give his/her consent to authorise Bolt to deduct the sum from the user’s elected payment method;
# If the user gives his/her consent, then Bolt deducts the sum from the user’s elected payment method. CASE CLOSED\!
# According to the T&C-s the user has 10 days to challenge the fine/contractual penalty and has 14 days to give Bolt authorisation to deduct the sum or make the outstanding payment him/herself. Within these 14 days the user can continue using Bolt Services.
# If the user does not make the authorization with 14 calendar days, then Bolt has following alternatives:

a)       Bolt is entitled to not to allow the user to use any of Bolt’s services;

b)      if the user tries to use Bolt’s service, then then the user shall first pay the debt and only then the price of the service;

c)    claim late payment interest until the amount has been fully settled;

d)   assign this claim to a third party (for example, a debt collection company);

Bolt sends *Bolt in app notification* when 14 days due date has passed (see point 4 of the attached User Flow Notifications). With this approach we basically “force” the user to give us consent or pay the fine/penalty if they want to continue using Bolt services (BD, RH, food, delivery, scooters). If the user gives the consent/continues using service, then Bolt deducts the sum, e.g. by adding this to the next service fee. CASE CLOSED\!

If the user does not make the authorization and do not use Bolt services anymore, then Bolt can use alternatives c) and d) simultaneously: sends another claim to the user’s email with late payment interest and, if needed, assigns the claim to a third party debt collection company (we are currently using Julius Inkasso services). *NB\!* +Is it possible or what is the likelihood that the user will deactivate the account and creates a new one for avoiding paying the fine and continuing using service?+

     7. In case the user challenges the traffic fine/contractual penalty, then Bolt should evaluate all the      circumstances case-by-case (if necessary, please seek legal advice by submitting legal ticket to SD) and if the Bolt cannot prove the user’s fault or the violation itself, Bolt shouldn’t claim for the fine or contractual penalty.

------

**What kind of fines/penalties/damages can be covered with this approach?* Main ATTN: [~accountid:60acee2e317edd00718c5650] 

*I) Traffic fines* (speeding camera fines, traffic light fines, parking violations) issued by the state authorities, usually by police. +Bolt must not pay such fines on behalf of users by default\!+ – this is only for cases where police are not able to identify the user, Bolt is unable to give relevant personal details to police (e.g. user name is Super Mike, invalid email address, etc). Only then can Bolt decide to pay the fine on behalf of the user and reclaim it from the user.

+Legal risks:+ From legal point of view such fines are called cautionary penalties and are issued under Estonian Code of Misdemeanor Act for traffic misdemeanours. According to laws, Bolt is not obliged to fulfil the obligation and/or has a right to object the fine/penalty addressed to Bolt - the User is the obligated person for the relevant fine. However, as I understand from BD ops team, Bolt wants to keep good relationship with police and therefore has “voluntarily” accepted to pay the fines.

The obligatory party is the user and under the law the users have the right to contest such fine. If the fine is contested, then it does not enter into effect. Therefore, if Bolt “voluntarily” pays such fines, then with such action Bolt deprives the user from his/her lawful right to contest the claim. Therefore, BD team should carefully consider all the circumstances of alleged infringement done by the user before paying the fine on behalf of the users.

If Bolt has paid the fine on behalf of the users, request authorization (according to the user flow above) to deduct the fine form the user’s payment method, but the users contest Bolt’s claim and is able to prove that there was no infringement (e.g. the traffic light was out of order), then Bolt cannot claim the fine from the user already paid by Bolt to police.

*II) Parking fines for failing to pay for parking in public parking areas* in the meaning of Estonian Road Traffic Act. This is for cases where parking in public parking areas is not covered by Bolt Drive service fee.

*III) Parking fines for parking in (paid) private parking areas* which are not covered by Bolt Drive service fee.

Such parking fine is considered as contractual penalty imposed by a third-party legal entity (e.g. Europark, AS Ühisteenused for parking in car parks (in Estonian: parkimismajad) which are not public parking areas) in the meaning of Estonian Laws of Obligations Act. From legal point of view Bolt is not obligatory party to pay such fines. The contractual penalty is an obligation which is prescribed in the “parking contract” and under which the party which fails to perform the contract undertakes to pay an amount of money determined by the contract to the other party. However, Bolt is not a party to this contract since the acceptance to conclude the parking contract is given by driving the vehicle to the parking lot, which means acceptance is given by the user of the vehicle. Therefore, Bolt can object the contractual penalty on the ground that Bolt was not the user of the vehicle at the time stated in the penalty notice.

However, in order to avoid possible conflicts with private parking areas, and to keep good relationships with them, we have adjusted BD T&C-s so that if the user fails to pay for the private parking areas and parking fine is issued, then it is considered as a violation of BD T&C’s (a contract between the user and Bolt) which means that we can claim contractual penalty from the user in the amount of unpaid parking fee. In such case you can settle the parking fine for parking in the private parking area directly with the car park (i.e third party legal entity).

*IV) A contractual penalty established by Bolt* which the User is obliged to pay to Bolt pursuant to the BD T&C and list of penalties (for whatever contractual infringement);

*V)* *A contractual claim for compensation for damage to Bolt* – e.g. the User sets the car on fire (for no good reason) and Bolt suffers damages.

-------

Please let me know if you have any questions, concerns or something needs specifying and let me know your thoughts. We can also schedule a meeting if its more convenient.

Best regards

Häli

+A+ +*new temporary regime*+ +was adopted in Brussels just before Christmas. That brought a number of changes in the approach for our ride-hailing operations launch in Brussels (ETA adjusted to 1st Feb)+:

* The temporary solution will only benefit LVC drivers who obtained their license prior to 15 Jan 2021. So LVC drivers who obtained their license after 15 Jan 2021 would still be subject to the 1995 Regulation.
* *Riders Association (RA) no longer needed*, at least not in order to try to comply with the 1995 Regulation.
* Business decision not to keep the RA just for the benefit of the LVC drivers mentioned above (who obtained their license prior to 15 Jan 2021).
* Outside counsel confirmed that the RA would not offer any administrative advantages for Bolt. Therefore it exists but we won’t use it.
* Decision was taken to launch on the basis of the temporary regime and then switch to compliance with the Pan Taxi when it comes into force.

+The new Temporary Regime sets out 3 requirements+:

* Have an *establishment unit* in Belgium registered in the Belgian company register \[_avoir, en Belgique, une unité d’établissement enregistrée à la Banque-Carrefour des Entreprises_]
* Make an *electronic taxi reservation service* available to the public \[_mettre à la disposition du public un service de réservation électronique de services de taxis_]
* *Allow the administration to access electronically the following information, which must be permanently updated*: driver/operator T&Cs, which must not restrict affiliation to other platforms or foresee increased costs in that case,  customer T&Cs, identification data of registered drivers and operators \[_permettre à la direction Transport de Personnes de Bruxelles Mobilité d’accéder électroniquement aux informations suivantes, mises à jour en permanence : a) les données d’identification des exploitants et des chauffeurs enregistrés sur la plateforme ;) les conditions générales d’affiliation à la plateforme applicables aux exploitants et aux chauffeurs, lesquelles ne peuvent ni leur interdire de s’affilier également à d’autres plateformes de leur choix, ni imposer de surcoût à ceux qui s’affilient à plusieurs plateformes ; c) les conditions générales d’utilisation de la plateforme applicables aux clients_]

* Outside Counsel recommended to *set up an Establishment Unit*, as required by the new temporary regime.

I think the correct way to solve it is the following:

* getActiveBasket also returns the menu id
* when app enters the same provider’s menu as the active basket, it will compare those two menu ids
* if menu ids are different, the app should call getBasketSummary which will do the basket migration and the menu is fetched (at the same time getBasketSummary should also return the menu id)

The tricky part is how to solve the first bullet. From BE we have two ways of doing this:

* save the menu id in the db (which involves, making a new column, db infra, updating models, updating tests etc. - just to point out that is time-consuming)
* get the menu id on demand (on get active basket endpoint) from delivery-search/delivery-provider services. In this case we have to measure the performance a bit because we also noticed some spike [alerts|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/GQ3NRL18T/p1641987876002400?thread_ts=1641987475.001800&cid=GQ3NRL18T] on this endpoint . Dear Sir/Madam

Bolt recognises the legitimate interests in making necessary and proportionate disclosures to the police and law enforcement agencies in order for the authorities to undertake statutory law enforcement functions. Bolt usually relies on the UK GDPR legitimate interest lawful basis in order to facilitate such disclosures. For legitimate interests to prevail, and to satisfy the condition, Bolt must undertake the associated assessment. 

On completion of the assessment, it is concluded that Bolt cannot lawfully make the disclosure as proposed by the police. 

First, on the test of necessity, the disclosure of the data of all users who have used Bolt service from or to that address is not the only means to identify people living at this address. Furthermore, we do not hold information about the residents of that address. 

Second, on the test of proportionality, the disclosure fails to relate to any other personal identifier (even the fact that any suspects have been identified to use Bolt service). Upon disclosure we would be disclosing irrelevant user data which have no connection to the investigation. Therefore, on the assessment of balance, individual’s legitimate interests, and the right of privacy, override the legitimate interests of the police request.

I’ll try to explain the history and reasoning behind this request and answer the questions. 

Firstly, this blocking option was the one we had used previously. It is the block “Other” where we can write a custom blocking reason. In the past, we used “Pending investigation, please refer to your messages”. This is used for the passengers at the moment as well. All Customer Safety Support agents have this access already.


Why this is needed? In order to differentiate the investigative blocks and blocks where the case itself has been closed, but we are leaving the user suspended without a consequential block being placed. Currently, we review the blocked drivers once a month on a spreadsheet to see if we can remove any of the suspensions and allow the drivers back on the road. Having two separate suspensions will eliminate the need to do so, or at the very least reduce the number of driver profiles to review. 
Secondly, this will help report the Customer Safety Support team’s health up the chain. For example, we can get correct numbers on average hours a driver is suspended due to an investigation and how many drivers are suspended over 48h (to prioritise and have an indication, when FTE needs to be increased)

Additionally, I would hope there is a possibility to add a section in the investigational tool, when the option “Driver remains suspended” is selected, the tool would display the exact wording that is needed to copy-paste in the custom blocking reason.

* As explained in the first point, if the agents have the reason in front of them and they can copy-paste it to admin, it should not create any issues.

[~accountid:5cd9daa0bc70090d6ce26227] [~accountid:61445ecbe057c6006a5163cc] External counsel confirms that the 30-days rule applies to all premises. However, as mentioned before, these 30 days commence after the submission of _a complete and factually correct motion_ to the construction supervisory authority.

 One of the required attachments is a certificate on compliance of the intended use with the local spatial plan. If there is no local spatial plan in force (for the area where certain premises is located), the decision on the development conditions must be attached. This results from the fact, that under Polish zoning law, a change of use, requires issuing an administrative decision on the development conditions. According to their experience, issuing of this decision (i.e. decision on the development conditions concerning the change of use of the premises) should take up to 3 months (the above timeframe may vary due to pandemic constraints, however from their perspective such proceedings should not last 12 months).

 Please find below a short step-by-step guide regarding the change of use procedure:

# +*Preparation of the motion and completion of the required attachments*+

The first step is to prepare the complete motion to the construction supervisory authority. As requested, attached is the template of the motion (in Polish). 

[^Change of use - motion template.docx]

Below you can find also find a list of the mandatory attachments:

A.     Description and drawing specifying the location of the building;

B.     Concise technical description of the building;

C.     Statement about the right to dispose of the real property for construction purposes;

D.     Certificate on compliance of the intended use with the local spatial plan or in the absence of the local spatial plan the decision on the development conditions;

Depending on the intended use, it might be also necessary to enclose:

A.     Technical report;

B.     Permits, approvals and opinions which are obligatory under the provision of the Polish law (e.g. environmental decisions);

C.      An opinion of a fire protection expert.

+2.+ +*Verification of formal requirements*+

 The building supervisory authority will check the motion. If the motion has deficiencies or mistakes, the authority will ask you to remove the defects.

 3. +*Resolving the issue – change of use*+

 If your application meets all the requirements, the building supervisory authority will accept the change of use motion with so-called silent approval, meaning that you can change the use under the condition that the authority did not issue an objection within 30 days counted from the submission of the complete motion.

[~accountid:6026964fce2bee006a50a166] Regarding a +*summary of the claim, circumstances and legal guidance for our broker and insurers*+, please see below:

* A lady, *Mrs Yasmine BENHISSEN* (Mrs B) booked a car through the Bolt app in Paris on 28 Nov 2021. The name of the driver was *Yanis*. When she got in the car, the driver was wearing a cap.
* According to Mrs B, the driver was holding his phone on his hands and supposedly driving fast and then hit a traffic light. Apparently the accident was violent and the windows got broken and the airbags inflated. Supposedly, the driver left the car with Mrs B inside. A passerby helped her to leave the car. The Police and an ambulance came.
* We could confirm that on 2021-11-28 at 21:38:08 the driver "Yanis" started the journey with the client Yasmine. The trip ended at 22:00:22 - however not at the destination previously entered by Yasmine. It appears that this is the last time Yanis drove through our platform.
* We also confirm that *Yanis Djennad* is one of our registered driver. He was registered on our platform on 27 novembre 2020, and works through a *fleet owner* (Flotte Fleche Express, which registered with Bolt on 17 juillet 2019 and has 7 active drivers currently working through our app).
* Mrs B claims that she suffers physical injuries as well as moral prejudice. She ended up 23 days in sick leave. We are awaiting to receive proof of this.
* The Police informed her that it was a *fake VTC driver - Karim CHIBHI* - who was neither a professional driver nor a licensed driver, and not Yanis, the VTC driver mentioned in her Bolt booking.
* Mrs B filed a complaint against Mr Karim CHIBHI.
* Her lawyer sent us a letter dated 5 Jan (that we received by email) to inform us of the above. They are basing the *claim under Art. 3142-3 of the French Transport Code* ("_The booking platform shall be automatically liable to the customer for the proper performance of the obligations arising from the contract of carriage, whether or not this contract has been concluded at distance and whether these obligations are to be performed by the booking platform itself or by another service providers, without prejudice to the booking platform's right of recourse against them. However, the booking platform may be exonerated from all or part of its liability by proving that the non-performance or poor performance of the contract is attributable either to the client, or to the unforeseeable and insurmountable act of a third party unrelated to the provision of the service provided for in the contract, or to force majeure_").
* Her lawyer is affirming that "the non-performance of the obligation of safety arising from the transport contract is attributable to the VTC driver named Yanis initially working for your company, who sold his BOLT driver account to Mr Karim CHIBHI who does not hold a driving licence and does not work as a professional driver. Consequently, your company cannot exonerate itself from all or part of its responsibility and Mrs Benhissen's loss resulting from the non-fulfilment of your obligation of safety must be compensated."
* They are *open to an amicable resolution of this dispute within 15 days*, otherwise they will go to court. *No amount is mentioned in the letter*.
* On our side, we got confirmation that our Client High Priority Service Team (HP Team) received a message from Mrs B on Nov 29, 2021 at 21:06 informing us of the incident she had experienced the day before during her Bolt trip with "Yanis" (“who did not look like Yanis and who fled the scene of the accident, leaving her in an overturned vehicle, from which she got out thanks to the help of witnesses”). 13 minutes later, contact was made with her, but unfortunately our HP Team was unable to reach her again to discuss further the following day (but a message was left on her voicemail). Other unanswered phone calls followed as well as an exchange of short written messages. 
In parallel, our HP Team also tried to reach Yanis and the fleet owner a number of times but without any luck.
* +I have instructed Osborne Clarke Paris (OC) to assist us with this claim. They have advised as follows+:
** In their view,  *Bolt is liable on the basis of Art. 3142-3 of the French Transport Code*, as the transport service is being considered as provided by the booking platform and Bolt cannot rely on any of the (few) cases of exoneration provided.
** It appears from Mrs B's lawyer letter that *the victim filed a complaint against Karim Chibhi, so normally a criminal investigation will be conducted and may be extended* to Yanis Djennad and his fleet manager, but also *potentially to Bolt*. In this respect, the fact of settling with the victim for compensation does not prevent the State from prosecuting the persons whom they consider responsible for the disturbance caused to the order of society. However, in criminal matters, it is necessary to demonstrate the intention to commit the offence and in the case of Bolt a deliberate imprudence, negligence or endangerment of others. They have not identified any case law that has held a booking platform criminally liable. 
** +Based on the above, OC recommend to+:
** 1. *report this claim to our insurance company* and enquire whether our insurer want to involve one of their lawyers.
** 2. *acknowledge receipt of the letter* to Mrs B’s lawyer.
** 3. *start confidential negotiations between the lawyers to determine Mrs B's compensation*. This will require the analysis of the medical documents that will be provided and often the intervention of an expert doctor.
** 4. *forward the letter from Mrs B's lawyer to the driver and the fleet owner,* characterising their faults and contractual breaches, requesting their guarantee for the compensation that Bolt will have to pay to the victim and for the costs incurred *and to suspend their account* and notify them of our wish to terminate the contract.
** 5. Regarding the *criminal investigation* that is expected to follow (though we haven’t heard from the Police yet), OC is currently exploring the opportunity for Bolt to file a criminal complaint against Karim Chibhi - or if possible to join the victim’s claim and whether this would protect Bolt’s interests. They are awaiting to review Mrs B' complaint file to finalize their analysis.

Background information for Maria. This assignment was cancelled as it took too much time to prepare the necessary agreements. The agreements are still WIP (due to some invoicing dispute we had with Chinese lawyers) and should be finalized quite shortly.

*Background*: FACTORY manufactures END-PRODUCTS (e-scooters) for BOLT. SUPPLIER manufactures PRODUCTS (e.g. motor) for the FACTORY, which are used ultimately in our END-PRODUCTS. FACTORY purchase PRODUCT’S PARTS (e.g. motor components) from a THIRD PARTY. Currently, BOLT has a contractual relationship with the FACTORY for manufacturing end-products. BOLT has no direct relationship with the SUPPLIER.

*Proposed transactions (approximate total value 18 MEUR):* Due to worldwide shortage of specific PRODUCT’S PARTS, BOLT wants to ensure the availability of these PRODUCT’S PARTS in case of a need for the future manufacturing of building new scooters.

Two types of agreements where prepared:

One is for supply of Products and Product’s Parts (except battery materials) called “Tripartite Agreement”; the other is for supply of battery’ components (i.e. battery materials) called “Battery Agreement”.

+Tripartite Agreement+: there are three contracting parties: Bolt, Factory and Supplier. Bolt will not only buy the End-Products (scooters) from the Factory but also will obtain the ownership title of the Products that are used in the End-Products (from Supplier) and Product’s Parts (from 3^rd^ Vendor) respectively. The price for purchasing the Products will be paid through the Factory (as prepayment for End-Products) to the Supplier while the price for purchasing the Product’s Parts will be paid through the Factory, the Supplier in sequence (as prepayment for Products) and then to the 3^rd^ Vendor. The ownership of Products and Product’s Parts passes to Bolt.

+Battery Agreement+: Bolt will enter into a contract with the supplier to purchase batteries’ cells and other parts of batteries from the supplier directly. Bolt is not purchasing or obliges to purchase ready-made batteries from them. The payment for the batteries’ cells and other parts of batteries will be made from Bolt Estonia to the supplier directly.  Some batteries will be delivered to Europe, but it is also likely that some batteries will be stored in China for manufacturing by Chinese factory.  The ownership of the battery components passes to Bolt and we are securing the part of the batteries for later battery production by the supplier or another supplier if Bolt decides so.

Our tax advisors Deloitte raised concern about the payment flow in the Tripartite Agreement and enforceability of Bolt’s ownership over Products, Product’s Parts and battery components. This question was analyses by RuiBaiLaw Firm and it was confirmed that it is legally enforceable, however some changes need to be made to the agreement.

The agreements are WIP and will be stored in google drive, Legal Team folder, Hardware/Legal subfolder (link here). Other background info is also stored there.

Connection to MQTT broker and subscribing to a topic was implemented using KMM as a cross platform technology. MQTT handling in this prototype is provided by [Hive MQ|https://github.com/hivemq/hivemq-mqtt-client] on Android and [CocoaMQTT|https://github.com/emqx/CocoaMQTT] on iOS. There was implemented two wrappers over these 3d party libraries in order to use a single interface in a shared library. The whole business logic, including caching messages in the local DB and making additional network requests to fetch chat history, can be put in this shared library written in Kotlin. 

!KMM-MQTT-Demo.mp4|width=3920,height=2304!

KMM gradle plugin compiles the library code to JVM bytecode for Android and to LLVM bytecode for iOS. Interoperability between iOS Swift/Objective C code and KMM Kotlin code does not require any wrappers or bridges, Kotlin classes can be easily created and called in Swift and vice versa. There is a limitation in working from Kotlin with Swift/Objective C code: it should be from the standard iOS framework SDK or from a library that does not have any transitive dependencies (a library that depends only on the iOS framework). So if we need to deal with a platform dependent 3d party library in our KMM library we should provide Kotlin interfaces and implement them in Swift instead (i.e. Swift calls Kotlin and not vice versa).

KMM can also [be compiled to JS|https://kotlinlang.org/docs/js-overview.html#use-cases-for-kotlin-js] in order to use the common business logic in Web (or Mobile Web) applications, but this feature wasn’t tried and tested in the current POC.

Thank you for preparing it on time, Rita\! Some feedback on the project plan.

*Expected outcome:*

* New leadership workshops is rather a deliverable. See outcome as the ultimate benefits of the project: workshops are definitely benefits, yet they are just one of the steps to reach smth bigger. For example, better engagement is ultimate - it does not contribute to anything further, yet many things (such as new leadership workshops) would contribute to better engagement.

*Deliverables:*

* I feel onboarding can also be part of something a bit bigger. For example, if you phrase it as “Selected and trained project team OR team of instructors” this will be a more broad deliverable, yet it will also include whole selection and onboarding. This would help you in planning the project into milestones: basically, each of the deliverables should be included there.
* The second point is also too specific: try to simplify it. It does not mean that you will not have those files and sheets, yet when you want to present the program - you would avoid every little detail.
* TB Courses is enough as a deliverable - just like before, you would still have the registration, feedback etc. but the *key* deliverable is the TB Course.
* 4th point can fall under second - basically, all these sheets and events are about the organisation of the program, so you can merge them.
* I would also suggest rephrasing for simplicity. e.g. Impact Analysis - this included feedback and the rest.
* One great way of validating the deliverables is to critically review the list of expected outcomes. Is every outcome addressed in the deliverables or smth is missing? If the latter, think about what else could be added. At the moment, though, everything is good - as each outcome is addressed 🙂 

*Main stakeholders:*

* What about the communication with the TLs as participants? Where and how often will the communication happen?

*Success metrics:*

* 4 and 6 points are the same.
* Numbers are great for context, yet more valuable metrics are usually in %. For example, it is great to monitor the # of participants to understand how broad the program has been, yet measuring the % of all TLs participating can show how popular the program actually is. 
* I would also suggest looking at the # and % of the “returning” participants, basically the Leads who take part in more than 1 (or even all) the workshops.

*References:*

* I would also add the Confluence page here as it is relevant to the project. [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/3623092284/Leaders+Round+Table|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/3623092284/Leaders+Round+Table|smart-link] 



*General comments and feedback:*

* Check the project retro I put together last year - I left there some recommendations in the Start-Stop-Continue format at the end. See if you would like to implement something new to make the program more impactful. If so, definitely include it in the milestones.
* I see you have added a checklist - I would suggest using tasks instead. For example, you can have a task to create all necessary tools and then you would add a registration sheet, workshops calendar etc. as a checklist. Once you complete each of the points in the checklists, you can tick the task off meaning that all the necessary tools are ready.

I was just reading about spaced activities - they help people practice performing a task or retrieve information in sessions which are spaced days or weeks apart.

I know that this project is still on a very early stage and you first need to carefully investigate root causes of this issue. However, I thought that this idea is still worth sharing.

The underlying reason behind spaced activities is that one time training can barely improve performance. Learners can’t remember everything just from one session. We want to change their behavior and that requires time, thus we learn best when we practice a skill or a task repeatedly with some time between sessions in a safe environment where we are free to fail.

(I didn’t come up with that myself, it’s from Map it book).

It got me thinking about this project because we keep hearing about wrong SD escalations every now and then. Your solution will of course depend on the root causes of that but perhaps, you’d like to consider introducing spaced activities. 

Those could be simple quizzes in the TB with realistic examples of tickets where agents would have to decide where to escalate a ticket. This would help them practice making decisions that they have to make on the job basically every day. If we have several of such activities in intervals (e.g. every two weeks for 3 months, after which we would check if incorrect escalations reduced), that could help agents e.g. build a habit of checking KB articles and increase their confidence in decision making.

Let me know what you think.

* Description of how prelive nightly sync works
* We are currently managing 44 sandbox machines
* Each sandbox machine uses ZFS as a filesystem and hosting 3 MySQL instances ( Source of live data( AFA main MySQL ) / prelive / test ) using LXD container
* Every night at 3 am UTC, a cronjob will execute the following steps to provide nightly sync
* 
{noformat}1. Backup prelive & test users from prelive / test MySQL instances
2. Stop all 3 MySQL instances
3. Destory ZFS filesystems for prelive & test data
4. Create a ZFS snapshot of Main MySQL
5. Create ZFS clones of prelive / test using snapshot of Main MySQL
6. Start up all MySQL instances
7. Restore prelive & test users from prelive / test MySQL instances{noformat}



Concerns point 1.

Because we are hosting 3 MySQL instances in a single EC2 instance, sandbox machines are one of the most unstable MySQL EC2 instances so far.

Most of the time when sandbox EC2 instances fail because of overhead or malfunction of ZFS file system due to heavy writing and changes in disk level. Usually, DBAs need to re-create sandbox machines every month.

 Enabling prelive binlog will increase of writing and changes of sandbox EC2 instances and it will cause a more unstable situation and it lead to more frequent rebuild of sandbox EC2 machine.



Concern point 2.

There will be changes in GTID set in during the nightly.

Because we have 3 different MySQL instances ( Main MySQL / prelive / test )

Each MySQL has a different GTID set because each MySQL instances are all masters.

During the steps of No.3 to No.7, prelive GTID set will be overridden to Main MySQL’s GTID so there is a possibility of a pipe-breaking situation in Kafka every night.



This is why the decision of data copy is important to us. If there in no need of sync of data from Live, all those steps won’t be necessary and DBA won’t need ZFS, LXD and prelive will be served in a single EC2 instance and it won’t cause any performance problem or pipe-breaking situation or rebuilding.

Hi Sten,

Because not everyone is required to send image of taximeter, and as I mentioned, we’ve been told to keep the registration process as quick and easy as possible for the drivers, to get them into our funnel. As taximeter is one of the biggest barriers for drivers, having this as a requirement in the registration process, will potentially lead them not registering. 

We are in contact with Halda, which is a taximeter provider, that we can link the drivers to. So if the drivers register, with all the required documents, we can help them obtaining a taximeter to get going. 

We do also give the drivers 7 days to send the proof, or they’ll be blocked saying “Send a picture of your taximeter in order to get unblocked” which has been a success, [Overview of taximeter|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SR33VQdPH84aAreUQunqn91KENZYuB5gtD9Pf6MrVTM/edit#gid=0].

This is not something that is or should be handled by the CS-team. This is not OPS handing a task over to CS. It’s simply a guide on how to do a comment on a registrations and showing how we’re solving Taximeter tickets. So if the CS team sees a ticket like this, they know how we are doing this, and can do it directly them selves. This has been discussed with our CS team.

Basically, it’s just copy/pasting a link of the taximeter ticket over to the registration, so we OPS can take it from there. 

The guide can also be used as a training guide for new OPS agents.

Regards

Martin

Hi [~accountid:5e6b55b518039c0cf3f19c12] please see below the comments from externals regarding 14.2 and 14.3, before our discussion later. 

+*14.2*+

 We have noticed that landlords sometimes try to include such clauses in lease agreements, but it is not the market standard. Usually in the event of termination of the lease agreement due to tenant’s fault, the parties agree on a contractual penalty in the amount of 6 or 12 months of rent (but not more than the amount of rent which would be due from the date of termination until the end of original term of lease) plus proportion of Landlord’s contribution in the fit-out costs. 

 Pursuant to the Polish Civil Code, upon termination of the lease, the obligation to pay the rent ceases. As regards compensation – the parties may agree on contractual penalty (in this case the amount of contractual penalty is independent of the damage), or the Landlord may sue for losses due to early termination of the lease (in this case the Landlord must prove the amount of damage).

 +*14.3*+

Pursuant to Article 682 of the Polish Civil Code, if the defects of the leased premises are of such a kind that they endanger the health of the lessee or its employees, the lessee may terminate the lease without notice, even if he knew about the defects at the time of concluding the lease agreement.

This provision is imperative, which means that this principle cannot be excluded by the parties, so you are already protected in case of defects that threaten the life or health of the employees.

Another provision of the Civil Code that entitles the lessee to terminate the lease without notice is a situation where the subject of the lease has defects which prevent the agreed use of the subject of the lease and the lessor did not remove such defects in a timely manner despite being notified, or if the defects cannot be removed.

Please note that the standard in Poland is to rely on the provisions of the Civil Code with minor modifications. Sometimes it is possible to negotiate additional grounds for termination (for example if the same defect of the premises recurs or specific part of the premises, such as server room, has been destroyed), but in our view the Landlord’s proposal regarding termination of the lease meets the current market standard for office buildings.

Best, 

Liisa

Hi [~accountid:5eec86e8868ce30ac4bf5656], thanks for the ticket. 

First, if the cases are HP you *have to* follow to general workflow articles ([regular|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4411904921234], [significant|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4413546378002]) as they have been put in place by the Risk & Safety team and they are the ultimate authority when it comes to HP cases. 

When it comes to blocks the tool tells you what to do - if the case was Significant, it will advise you to block the courier (or any other offending party) for the duration of the investigation (the so-called _Investigative block)._ If the Tool recommends you to place it, do so without hesitation. If the Tool doesn’t recommend the investigative block, you should not block the courier while the investigation is ongoing since the offence is not serious enough. 

Secondly, there is absolutely no reason to consult with other team members or anyone else on how long the block should be, as the Tool also tells you that. Please make sure not to deviate from the tool’s recommendations as they’ve been put into place by the Risk & Safety team after careful consideration. 

Third, there is a whole process for contacting the offending party - it’s described in both articles. For regular cases, they are not to be contacted. Again, please abide by that. For Significant cases, they are to be contacted three times in the span of 72 hours, once every 24 hours. Only then you can presume their guilt. The article also tells you what you can or cannot share during the conversation. 

And finally - it was decided by the Risk & Safety team, Knowledge Management & CS STLs that OS agents should handle Regular HP cases. They should be able to handle them themselves without any assistance or asking for permission to place/lift blocks, as the tool takes care of all of that. 

For cases that are not HP, there is the [global blocking guide|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MN5J9rr_mEY4e2VbGWqUKrOtvzaWuUZYFghtBwic6PQ/edit#gid=1032727751] for couriers which should still be followed. We are currently having the Global OPS team review it & all changes will be announced to CS. 

Hope this answers your questions. Please let me know if I can close the ticket.

Blacklisting the user, the cards, or the device will just increase the score, which will push the user into 3ds flow. However, if the abuse is on refunds, the user won’t mind passing 3ds. Refund abuse does exist and is quite tricky to determine if a user is actually an abuser or if the person has a legitimate case of refund. Some feedback on the project plan:

*Desired outcome:*

* Increased growth driver is a way to understand whether we have achieved the success but what would be the ultimate outcome? What would an increased growth driver give us? Is it better performance, career growth etc? Basically, the Desired Outcome is a bigger goal (similar to vision) whereas Success Metrics is what exactly should happen for you to consider the project a success, hence the vision being achieved.

*Deliverables:*

* Will the project plan increase the growth factor? 🙂 It is a must for any project but what in particular will get you where you want with this project?
* I would merge points 2 and 3 as they independently do not have a value (e.g. just having questions ready OR just having sessions without proper questions won’t help you “identify and prioritise growth needs”. Think of it as one deliverable that would have two elements.
* What would be the purpose of the confluence page? Is it to be transparent on the outcomes of the listening sessions analysis? If so, it can be merged with point 5 as they are inter-connected.
* Potentially, you can merge all the last 4 points into one and treat it as a Listening sessions deliverable that includes:
** Questionnaire design
** Listening sessions
** Feedback analysis
** Confluence page with follow-up actions

*Main stakeholders and comms:*

* Will the communication be different with Agents and Leads? e.g. different channels, frequency? If so, it should be documented.
* In the deliverables, you mentioned the confluence page which is also a communication channel. How do you plan to use it?
* In the timeline you mentioned CS AH - it is also a comms channel.

*Success metrics:*

* Feel free to include the final outcome of the goal (as per our roadmap exercise file, it is 8.5)
* I would also recommend narrowing it down to CS agents only. Otherwise, Growth score for all other roles would affect the objectivity of the measures.

*Timeline:*

* Depending on what you decide about the final list of deliverables, the timeline will depend on them. The project plan does not need to be included there as well as minor sub-tasks such as Confluence and CS AH presentation (which can be merged into a task Communications on the results).



*General feedback:*

* *Out of scope* is missing - think what can be potentially expected from us but we consciously decide not to do from the beginning. See the guidelines for reference [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/3678931594/Project+plans+for+Jira+epics|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/3678931594/Project+plans+for+Jira+epics|smart-link] 
* I initially expected the first sessions to be concluded by the end of January as there will probably be more workload coming from ALD and Bootcamps in Feb-Mar. Will let you decide whether to squeeze it in this month or stick to your proposed plan.

* _In general are we able to evaluate the desired trips based on the indicators provided, without checking every single ride manually?_
** I do have access to download the details of orders made during this period as a CSV file and there are the following fields also included in the file 
*** Pick-up address
*** Destination address (inserted in the app by the Rider whilst requesting the ride) 
*** Real destination address (the actual location where the Driver finished the ride)
*** Pickup latitude
*** Pickup longitude
*** Drop off latitude
*** Drop off longitude

* In light of these cells available to be used for filtering, we could try either of the two approaches: 1) filter based on keywords present in particular cells (so any possible way of Swieqi (this can be “Swieqi” or “Is-Swieqi” and Bugibba (this can be “Bugibba” or “San Pawl il-Baħar” (because Bugibba is a part of Saint Paul’s Bay) or “Saint Paul’s Bay”), As you can already tell, the main concern here is that the street names in Malta do not always appear consistently in Google Maps (and therefore also in our system). Moreover, the locality name seems to not always be present in the cells in question either. 
* The other way of filtering would be to limit the pick-up and destination latitude and longitude which my colleague helped me to do. I cannot confidently confirm that this filtering approach is also free of errors, but out of the two possible options, it seems to be more trustworthy. After doing this, we limited the orders down to *12.* 
* How many rides are affected (trips from Swieqi to Bugibba) in the requested time?
** As explained in the above bullet point, there are certain valid concerns about filtering the orders. *OHAS*: as a general rule, the specifics should be consulted with the health and safety officer (what are the risks, how they are mitigated, what PPE should be used etc). As a general rule - working in a dangerous/hazardous environment is not compensated in remuneration, but as rest time.  Transportation of batteries is generally not regarded as dangerous activity, but some restrictions may apply.

*Transportation*: batteries are classified as dangerous goods* if no exception is applicable. Special training of van drivers and marking on vans could be applicable. ADR sets an exception to the general rule - further analysis is needed. If the batteries are classified as dangerous, additional training to the driver operating the van is needed. NB\! This is only applicable to removable and/or lithium batteries.

[Internal redirects in Envoy|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/intro/arch_overview/http/http_connection_management#internal-redirects]
For a redirect to be handled successfully it must pass the following checks:


# Have a response code matching one of [redirect_response_codes|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-internalredirectpolicy-redirect-response-codes], which is either 302 (by default), or a set of 3xx codes (301, 302, 303, 307, 308).
# *Have a* *_location_* *header with a valid, fully qualified URL.*
# *The request must have been fully processed by Envoy.*
# The request must be smaller than the [per_request_buffer_limit_bytes|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-route-per-request-buffer-limit-bytes] limit.
# [allow_cross_scheme_redirect|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-internalredirectpolicy-allow-cross-scheme-redirect] is true (default to false), or the scheme of the downstream request and the _location_ header are the same.
# The number of previously handled internal redirect within a given downstream request does not exceed [max internal redirects|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-internalredirectpolicy-max-internal-redirects] of the route that the request or redirected request is hitting.
# All [predicates|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-internalredirectpolicy-predicates] accept the target route.

Any failure will result in redirect being passed downstream instead.

Since a redirected request may be bounced between different routes, any route in the chain of redirects that

# *does not have internal redirect enabled*
# or has a [max internal redirects|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-internalredirectpolicy-max-internal-redirects] smaller or equal to the redirect chain length when the redirect chain hits it
# or is disallowed by any of the [predicates|https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-internalredirectpolicy-predicates]

will cause the redirect to be passed downstream.

There is an issue in how we update existing fees in case import task is re-evaluated after commission change. Essentially we depend on existing {{total_fee_with_vat}} when calculating new fee {{sum_with_vat}} - at the same time {{sum}} is calculated independently based on {{total_ride_price}}. {{vat_sum}} is then calculated as difference of these two. As a consequence change of commission introduces a incorrect change in {{vat_sum}} for recalculated fees - depending on direction of commission change the change of {{vat_sum}} will be be positive or negative.

[~accountid:5bdc567ddabb7e15b08738ec] Yeah, it looks like I had misunderstood that the CS Product had a certain vision of how the KB content will be provided for agents with some sort of an automatized solution. But I see that I might have misunderstood this completely - therefore from now on, I am looking at KB content and formatting/structuring it as you mentioned: _to make them lean and easier to follow, thus, the need to support complex structured content will be eliminated._

*As for jump-to-links*, I have to admit I do not see how this makes the content easier to perceive and follow through. I don’t see how bulky KB content with hyperlink navigation would be lean and easier to follow. Jump-to links essentially fulfil the purpose as the Table of Contents do - which is different from the multiple purposes fulfilled by dropdowns in Bolt KB content. True, you can jump to the relevant section - however, seeing the whole block of content is way more overwhelming for the reader perception-wise than viewing an article where only the relevant information is in front of the eyes, with the less important information hidden in dropdowns. 

Additionally, I personally don’t yet see other solutions (than expandable/collapsible elements aka dropdowns) for _hiding certain parts of the content_ in order to direct the attention to what’s most important.

It can be argued that all of this is again at a _feelings_ level. However, this comes from my multiple years-long experiences of reviewing bulky, lengthy content and simplifying it with the help of basic formatting features like dropdowns, headings, etc. which are available in any KB tool that I’ve worked with already from the start or can be created with the help of HTML and CSS. I believe that we’re starting to go in circles in this discussion and that all concerns, pros and cons for both keeping and eliminating the expandable and collapsible elements (aka dropdowns) were weighed. It’s time to proceed to conclusions and determine the further action plan.

[~accountid:5a9eaf7ca00c7f2a80156a09] [~accountid:5ac5d648f222901f28965ee3] [~accountid:5cfa2e89757e4b0f2636ebf7] As I understand, *the objective of this task* is to explain to the CS Product team how we use dropdowns in the KB content  - however, from what we’ve discussed here already, it looks like it is up to them to provide knowledge of the implementation of dropdowns (as we know and use them in Zendesk), or sharing alternative solutions that would let the CS Content team achieve the same purposes as described above. 

*Here’s what we have learned through the Slack discussion and the conversations in the comments on this task:*

* Dropdowns fulfil the following purposes in our KB content:
** storing multiple scenarios under the bolded steps
** Storing less frequent scenarios at the bottom of the article
** storing multiple sub-processes in a single article
** Response templates or examples to explain a concept better
** FAQ at the bottom of the article
* The common theme across these different uses is placing less critical details in the background (so that they’re still available) and highlighting the essential steps of the process (so they’re easy to scan and follow).
* There needs to be some sort of functionality that allows CS agents to see in a KB article only the essential details at the first glance, and expand secondary details when necessary.
* The CS Content team should critically evaluate other formatting functionality alternatives that would fulfil the same purpose and not make the article content bulkier and more overwhelming (which would contradict our goal to create lean and easy to follow processes for our CS agents)
* The CS Content team is unaware of the technical limitations in Beehive so we are limited in discovering the solution alternatives to the HTML <div> elements in Zendesk (the expandable and collapsible elements aka the dropdowns)

At this point, I would appreciate the direction from you [~accountid:5ac5d648f222901f28965ee3] [~accountid:5a9eaf7ca00c7f2a80156a09] [~accountid:5cfa2e89757e4b0f2636ebf7]  to understand the next actions here. Sharing results of impact estimation based on Bucharest & Kyiv. The metric is incremental rides (from surge sessions) as percentage of total rides (from all sessions in marketplace).

* Bucharest (Tuesday & Friday):
** *1.0-1.6% incremental rides*
* Kyiv (Tuesday & Friday):
** *0.7-1.0%* *incremental rides*

The impact correlates with demand pattern in terms of time of day, so to achieve estimated impact, we need to execute well during peak-hours.



Notes:

* Assuming 100% probability that required drivers will reposition.
* Will depend on our execution & driver engagement
* Incremental rides are estimated using a conversion rate model based on sessions, drivers & surge multiplier.
* Repositioning logic groups surge demand by 10 min time window + geo cell combinations and counts the number of available drivers within 10 min driving distance in the previous time window.
** We don’t consider drivers who were in surged areas in previous time window or who would have ended up in target cell anyway.
** Most undersupplied sessions are considered first and amount of drivers to add is the minimum that maximises uplift in rides to added drivers ratio subject to upper bound on drivers.
** We don’t consider potential impact of additional drivers on surge multiplier.

*Legal Assessment + Action points*

* We currently (even without Best Offer) lack transparency on how we select default category for passenger and how do we rank them?
** Best offer makes this gap even more visible and we should take steps to give transparency in our T&Cs (driver + passenger):

** T&C updates though are not pre-requisite for a launch
* The issue and reasoning: given that categories (especially Economy vs Bolt) are currently the only way for Drivers to “set” their pricing, a driver picking an Economy category (going for a scale at a lower pricepoint) may have an expectation that cheapest category/price is always features and default and may be surprised that category is selected on other factors. +*Scope and application of Art 3142-3 of the Transportation Code:*+

Summary:

* The driver is liable on the basis of the 1985 Badinter law;
* The platform is liable on the basis of article 3142-3 of the Transportation Code; with limited causes of exoneration : force majeure, victim’s fault, third-party action.

→ The booking platform is indeed subject to an “obligation de résultat” with regard to the performance of the transport service. This concerns both accidents to passengers and damages to their property during transport. This obligation is very strong in order to ensure the protection of customers: it is a question of offering them an easily identifiable and solvent debtor of liability.
--> So Bolt is subject to an obligation to perform the ride without any accident but does have a *right of recourse against the driver and the fleet owner*. This right of recourse is based on the contract concluded between them.
--> Bolt also has a *right of recourse against the fake driver* on the basis of tort and/or criminal law.

Full scope analysis of article 3142-3 of the Transportation Code: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rIRKH5tNFHmRkNPRz1CYHa_UlZFdU_Bb/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rIRKH5tNFHmRkNPRz1CYHa_UlZFdU_Bb/edit|smart-link] 

I am surprised about the extent of our obligations as a platform in FR and I don't think this is something that we had truly appreciated before - therefore I have instructed another law firm - De Gaulle Fleurance et Associés (DGFLA) - for a second opinion on the scope and application of Art 3142-3, just to be 100% sure. I'm hoping to get that second opinion by EOW.
